_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#6, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: use ib_u.N for the velocity-block split because hard-coding nx*dim*2 gives 'off-by-one errors' where the DOF count depends on the element family. Ran: the naive vertices-times-dim count against basis.N for ElementVector over TriP1, TriP2, Quad1 and Quad2 on the same 8x8 tensor grid, then a deliberate split of an [u; p] vector at the naive index. Printed: 'OFF-BY-ONE' UNDERSTATES IT -- the largest discrepancy is 416 DOFs, more than a factor of three, because the formula counts vertices while P2/Q2 also carry edge DOFs. The formula is RIGHT for the P1 vector space on triangles and for Q1, which is what makes it dangerous: correct in the first case a reader tries and silently wrong the moment the element order changes. The consequence is silent -- splitting a 659-long vector at the naive index gives a 497-long 'pressure' slice against the true 81, with an empty warning list and 416 velocity entries pulled into the pressure block. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 makes split_index() return bu.N instead of the hand-derived (NX+1)**2*dim count, both in the per-space comparison and at the [u; p] cut -- the documented fix, ib_u.N. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 7 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'formula_is_wrong_for_at_least_one_space=True', 'discrepancy_exceeds_a_factor_of_three=True' and 'naive_split_contaminates_pressure=True' so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py FIXED 2026-08-08 (assertion changed): the vector being split was x = np.arange(total), and naive_split_contaminates_pressure was np.sum(bad_p[:len(bad_p)-bp.N] < bu.N) > 0. On an arange that reduces to the identity `index < bu.N`, worth exactly max(bu.N - cut, 0) for every mesh, every element and every physics -- it says nothing about a velocity or a pressure, and it merely restated tri_P2_naive_matches_basis_N=False, which is already asserted. The vector is now a real pair of FIELDS: a velocity projected onto the ElementVector space and a pressure projected onto P1, on separated value ranges (measured velocity_block_min_abs=8.9997, pressure_block_max_abs=1.0681), so 'came from the velocity block' is read off WHAT AN ENTRY IS, not off where it sits; velocity_and_pressure_value_ranges_separate is asserted so that premise cannot rot. A second, new assertion says how wrong the result is as a FIELD: the leading bp.N entries of the naive slice -- what downstream code reads as p[0], p[1], ... -- against the pressure that was actually projected, naive_pressure_field_relative_error=1.1203e+01. FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by reading: aligning that comparison on the TAIL of the slice instead compares vec[bu.N:] with itself and prints exactly 0.0000e+00 whatever the split did -- the same defect one level up, caught because the first version was executed. PROVEN: unmutated rc=0 with contaminates_pressure=True (416 entries) and field_is_wrong=True; T2_MUTATE=1 gives contaminated=0, relative error 0.0000e+00, field_is_wrong=False and rc=2.
